The rates/supply channel that dominated the Oct 2 read is improving (strong 10Y/30Y auctions, lower yields, MOVE and HY OAS easing), while the risk-off signal now sits in Asia equities and semis, with oil as an inflation-side wildcard. transmission.bottom_line: The Treasury supply test passed and long-end stress is easing, but the risk-off signal has moved to Asia and semis. Since the Oct 2 run the 30Y is 2.8bp lower at 5.605% (10bp above the 5.5% stress line, from 13bp) after the 10Y and 30Y reopenings cleared on 70-78% indirect demand; the 2Y fell 7.1bp, MOVE eased to 100.7 (from 107.6) and HY OAS to 3.09% (from 3.24%). Real yields are off their highs against flat breakevens, so oil's +3.53% jump (above the 3% flag) is read as a real-rate/supply story, not inflation. Offsets: VIX is 15.54, SOFR-IORB is -2bp and net liquidity is flat at ~$5.79T. New negatives: the Korea gate closed to 1/3 (EWY -4.28%, KOSPI -2.62%), semis sold off (SOXX -3.91%) and banks cut Treasury+agency holdings by $29.2B at the last H.8. The Treasury-demand module upgrades to Healthy (provisional); tonight's H.4.1 and tomorrow's H.8 are the next tests.
